Organic additives play an important role in regulating <sup>fi</sup>lm growth and properties in Cu electrodeposition.

celerators that promote Cu electrodeposition rate. In this study, the formal reduction potential of SPS to MPS wa

4. Conclusions
The formal reduction potential of SPS was <sup>fi</sup>rst determined by using
thiol–disulfide interchange reaction with ME and Lip. The calculated
formal reduction potential of SPS under the standard condition was
0.153 V (vs. SHE) in aqueous solution. The cell potential of the for-
mation of Cu(I)(thiolate) complexes, which is the key reaction to ex-
plain the accelerating mechanism, was also estimated based on the
formal reduction potential of SPS. The cell potential of Cu(I)(thiolate)
formation between
\mathrm { { C u } ^ { + } }
and SPS was 0.202 V, and the reaction between
{ \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }
and MPS was 0.214 V. We believe that the thermodynamic values
obtained in this study would be helpful in understanding or developing
industrial Cu electrodeposition involving SPS.

4. Conclusions
The formal reduction potential of SPS was <sup>fi</sup>rst determined by using
thiol–disulfide interchange reaction with ME and Lip. The calculated
formal reduction potential of SPS under the standard condition was
0.153 V (vs. SHE) in aqueous solution. The cell potential of the for-
mation of Cu(I)(thiolate) complexes, which is the key reaction to ex-
plain the accelerating mechanism, was also estimated based on the
formal reduction potential of SPS. The cell potential of Cu(I)(thiolate)
formation between
\mathrm { { C u } ^ { + } }
and SPS was 0.202 V, and the reaction between
{ \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }
and MPS was 0.214 V. We believe that the thermodynamic values
obtained in this study would be helpful in understanding or developing
industrial Cu electrodeposition involving SPS.
